question: Which project management system would best support a small remote executive team that needs clear task ownership, executive visibility, collaboration, documentation, and workflow automation?

sources.title: Asana Projects
sources.note: Asana supports tasks, project views, custom fields, rules, forms, status updates, and reporting dashboards. It also supports list, calendar, timeline, Gantt, and Kanban views.

sources.title: Asana Reporting Dashboards
sources.note: Asana provides project, portfolio, and universal reporting dashboards designed to give teams and executives a consolidated view of project progress and performance.

sources.title: Asana Starter Features
sources.note: Asana documents integrations with Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack and other tools, along with rules, forms, task dependencies, custom fields, and reporting.

sources.title: Notion Projects
sources.note: Notion combines project management with connected documentation, databases, timelines, tasks, dependencies, and customizable project information.

sources.title: Notion Databases
sources.note: Notion databases allow teams to organize information using customizable properties and multiple views including table, board, calendar, timeline, and chart.

sources.title: Notion Tasks and Dependencies
sources.note: Notion supports sub-items and task dependencies, including automatic date shifting when dependent tasks change.

sources.title: Linear Features
sources.note: Linear focuses on modern product development, with capabilities covering planning, projects, issue tracking, cycle planning, insights, customer requests, and AI-powered workflows.

sources.title: Linear Slack Integration
sources.note: Linear integrates closely with Slack, allowing users to create issues from Slack, synchronize conversations, receive notifications, and update issues from Slack.

key_findings: Asana provides the strongest executive-oriented project visibility of the three, with dashboards, portfolio reporting, custom fields, status updates, and multiple project views.
Asana is well suited to cross-functional teams because its workflow covers task ownership, deadlines, dependencies, reporting, forms, automation, and integrations.
Notion is the strongest option when documentation and project information need to live together. Its databases, pages, timelines, dependencies, and customizable views provide significant flexibility.
Notion requires more workspace design and configuration because teams can build their own workflows rather than adopting a more structured project-management system.
Linear is highly capable for product and engineering teams, particularly where issue tracking, cycles, roadmaps, and development workflows are central.
Linear's Slack integration is strong, but its product positioning is primarily around product development rather than general executive administration.
For a small remote executive team, executive reporting and cross-functional coordination are more important than specialized software-development workflows.

options.name: Asana
pros: Multiple project views including timeline and Gantt
Integrations with Slack and productivity tools
cons: Some advanced reporting capabilities require higher-tier plans
Less flexible than Notion for building a fully customized knowledge system
Can introduce more structure than a very small team may initially need

options.name: Notion
pros: Projects, tasks, documentation, and meeting information can coexist
Supports timelines, dependencies, multiple views, and automation
Strong flexibility for evolving team processes
cons: Highly flexible systems can become inconsistent without governance
Executive reporting is less purpose-built than Asana's dashboard approach

options.name: Linear
cons: Primarily designed around product and software development
Less suitable for general executive administration
May introduce unnecessary technical structure for a non-engineering executive team

unknowns: Actual user adoption and satisfaction within the specific executive team being evaluated
Total cost based on the team's required plan and number of users
How well each platform fits the team's existing Google Workspace, Gmail, Slack, and other workflows
Whether the team prioritizes centralized documentation enough to justify choosing Notion over a dedicated project-management platform
Whether the team has engineering or product-development responsibilities that would make Linear more valuable

recommendation.reason: Asana is the strongest overall fit for a small remote executive team because it combines structured task management, executive reporting, project visibility, workflow automation, and cross-functional collaboration without being primarily designed for software development.
recommendation.caveat: The recommendation is based on documented capabilities and fit against the stated requirements, not on a controlled user survey or hands-on trial.

next_action: Run a 7-day pilot using the same sample executive workflow in Asana and Notion, then compare setup effort, task adoption, reporting quality, documentation needs, and integration with the team's existing tools.
